=== APPROVED PRODUCT BRIEF (the user picked this from a 5-brief set; build EXACTLY this) ===

Frame: convention-honoring (probability 0.4)
Title: Trailblazer Match — A Copilot Workflow in Teams
Thesis: A first-year student opens Teams, sees three alumni matched to her exact CLR skill gaps, and accepts a Copilot-drafted intro in one click.
Why this frame: This is the defensible, IT-approvable shape: a Copilot agent surfacing SharePoint-indexed alumni inside Teams with double opt-in and Power Automate orchestration. It honors Liz's no-new-platform rule and Jen's M365-first mandate exactly as the engagement brief specifies.

PRIMARY PERSONA:
  Name: Maya Chen
  Role: First-year Computer Science undergraduate, Khoury College
  Context: Three weeks into CS 2500 (Fundamentals of CS I, Python). First co-op cycle opens in eight months. She is staring at a failed problem set and a NUworks tab full of postings she does not feel qualified for.
  Emotional state: Quietly anxious, comparison-spiraling on Reddit and Discord, embarrassed to ask faculty, suspicious that 'NU Source' is broken (her RA told her not to bother).
  Pain points:
    - Cannot tell which of her CLR skill gaps are normal first-year gaps versus disqualifying ones for co-op
    - Alumni at brand-name companies feel unreachable and intimidating — she does not know how to start a cold message
    - NU Source is dysfunctional and abandoned; she has no trusted channel to find relatable mentors
    - She lives in Microsoft Teams for coursework but has never seen the alumni network show up there
    - Generic advice from career services does not match her specific Python-week-4 struggle
  JTBD: When I am stuck on a first-year skill and unsure if co-op is realistic for me, help me find an alum who hit the same wall and pivoted out of it, so I can borrow their playbook without having to be brave first.
SECONDARY ACTORS:
  - Alumni Trailblazer (Sarah Okafor '22): Opted into the SharePoint-indexed alumni corpus, receives match invitations in Teams, sets weekly micro-volunteering capacity
  - Liz (Co-op Strategy Lead, NXT Humans engagement sponsor): Approves Copilot communication templates, monitors the Power BI outcomes view, manages adoption-burden risk
  - Jen (IT M365 Steering): Owns the cost-containment guardrail; reviews Azure OpenAI consumption, ensures no procurement of new platforms
  - IT M365 Admin (Under-the-Radar Innovator): Builds the Azure OpenAI semantic search, indexes the SharePoint CLR corpus, authors the Power Automate flow
  - Co-op Advisor: Sees Power BI outcomes dashboard, escalates flagged conversations, never sees the student's raw CLR gap data without FERPA opt-in

DEMONSTRATED MOMENT: Maya opens the 'Trailblazer Match' tab inside her Khoury Class of 2028 Team. Three alumni cards appear, each with an explainable rationale tied to her CLR profile. She taps Sarah '22 — 'hit the same Python wall in week 4' — confirms the FERPA double opt-in, and Copilot drafts a warm, specific intro message that posts to a new Teams thread within ninety seconds.

USE CASES (10) — the prototype MUST demonstrate at least 5 of these as live flows:
  1. CLR Gap Snapshot
     Trigger: Maya logs into Teams Monday morning; the Trailblazer Match tab shows a fresh weekly CLR pulse derived from her Canvas grades, Banner enrollment, and self-attested NUworks profile.
     Flow: Step 1: Tab loads with a Fluent 2 skill radar showing six CLR competency bands. Step 2: Two bands glow amber — 'Programming Fundamentals' and 'Professional Communication.' Step 3: Microcopy says 'This is normal for week 3 of CS 2500 — 71% of first-years are here too.' Step 4: A Match button appears with a count of available Trailblazers. Step 5: Maya taps Match.
     AI role: Gemini 3.1 Pro normalizes the multi-source signals into a CLR vector; Wiki RAG grounds the 'normal for week 3' comparative claim against historical Khoury cohort data indexed in SharePoint.
     Outcome: Maya feels seen, not deficient. The gap is reframed as a coordinate, not a verdict.
  2. Trailblazer Shortlist
     Trigger: Maya taps Match from the snapshot screen.
     Flow: Step 1: Loading state shows 'Searching 1,247 opted-in alumni in SharePoint…' with a shimmering Fluent skeleton. Step 2: Three match cards animate in, ranked by trajectory similarity not prestige. Step 3: Each card shows alum name, grad year, current role, similarity score, and a one-line rationale. Step 4: Maya can swap any card for the next-best alternate.
     AI role: Azure OpenAI embeddings perform cosine similarity over the CLR vector space; Claude Opus 4.7 writes the one-line rationale grounded in the matched alum's historical CLR record.
     Outcome: Three relatable humans appear where Maya expected a directory.
  3. Match Rationale Reveal
     Trigger: Maya taps a card to expand it.
     Flow: Step 1: Card flips, revealing a side-by-side CLR trajectory chart — Sarah's freshman year on the left, Maya's current state on the right. Step 2: Three specific overlap points highlight in amber. Step 3: A grounded paragraph explains the match in plain language with citations back to Sarah's opted-in CLR milestones. Step 4: A 'Why not these other alumni?' link reveals the negative space.
     AI role: Claude Opus 4.7 generates the rationale with explicit citations; Verbalized Sampling produces three candidate phrasings and the highest-confidence one is shown with the others available behind a 'Rephrase' affordance.
     Outcome: Maya understands why this match, not just that it exists. Trust shifts from 0 to workable.
  4. FERPA Double Opt-In Consent
     Trigger: Maya taps 'Connect' on Sarah's card.
     Flow: Step 1: A Fluent modal appears titled 'Before we introduce you to Sarah.' Step 2: Three plain-language checkboxes: share gap context, share enrollment year, allow Sarah to reply in Teams. Step 3: A FERPA footer states what is and is not shared. Step 4: Maya checks all three, taps Confirm. Step 5: A parallel consent request fires to Sarah; her acceptance is required before the thread is created.
     AI role: No generation here — deterministic Power Automate logic. Audit log written to SharePoint with cryptographic timestamp.
     Outcome: Maya feels in control of her data; the institution has a defensible audit trail.
  5. Copilot-Drafted Intro
     Trigger: Both opt-ins complete.
     Flow: Step 1: Copilot composer opens with a draft message already populated. Step 2: The message references the specific overlap ('Python week 4') and asks one warm, low-stakes opening question. Step 3: Maya can regenerate, edit inline, or accept. Step 4: A 'tone' slider offers warmer/more-professional variants. Step 5: Send posts to a new private Teams thread with both parties added.
     AI role: Claude Opus 4.7 drafts; Verbalized Sampling yields three tone variants (warm/balanced/professional) labeled with confidence; sensitive-content classifier (Gemini 3.1 Pro) blocks any draft that strays from approved templates.
     Outcome: Maya did not have to write the hard first message. She edited two words and hit send.
  6. Guided First Reply
     Trigger: Sarah replies in the Teams thread.
     Flow: Step 1: Maya sees Sarah's response. Step 2: A subtle Copilot chip appears under the compose box: 'Suggest a reply.' Step 3: Tapping it offers three prompt-starters grounded in Sarah's message ('Ask about her week-4 pivot,' 'Share your current problem set,' 'Ask how she found her fintech co-op'). Step 4: Maya picks one, edits, sends.
     AI role: Gemini 3.1 Pro reads only the in-thread context (not the CLR record) and proposes context-appropriate next moves.
     Outcome: The second message — historically the hardest — never becomes a bottleneck.
  7. Conversation Health Check
     Trigger: Background, daily.
     Flow: Step 1: A lightweight classifier scans the thread metadata (cadence, sentiment direction, message length) — not message content unless flagged. Step 2: If the conversation stalls past 10 days, a gentle nudge appears for Maya: 'Want Copilot to suggest a follow-up?' Step 3: If a sensitive-content flag fires, the thread is escalated to Liz's queue with no content shown to the advisor until Maya consents.
     AI role: Gemini 3.1 Pro for metadata classification; sensitive-content guardrail with human-in-the-loop escalation.
     Outcome: Conversations stay alive without becoming surveilled.
  8. Outcomes Dashboard for Liz
     Trigger: Liz opens the Power BI tab embedded in the Teams app.
     Flow: Step 1: Tab shows live KPIs — matches made, double opt-in rate, conversation activation rate, alumni engagement vs. NU Source baseline. Step 2: A cohort comparison chart shows the 100-student pilot against a control group. Step 3: A Copilot-summary panel auto-writes the weekly executive readout. Step 4: Export to PowerPoint for Liz & Jen's biweekly review.
     AI role: Claude Opus 4.7 writes the executive narrative grounded in the Power BI dataset.
     Outcome: Liz walks into her next stakeholder meeting with a defensible story.
  9. Alumni-Side Micro-Volunteer Inbox
     Trigger: Sarah opens her Teams app on Tuesday.
     Flow: Step 1: A 'Trailblazer Match' notification: 'A first-year hit the wall you remember — Maya, CS 2500, week 3.' Step 2: Sarah sees the requested time commitment (1 message/week, 4 weeks). Step 3: She taps Accept; the thread is created. Step 4: A small 'Set my capacity' control lets her cap inbound matches.
     AI role: Power Automate orchestrates the invitation; Claude Opus 4.7 writes Sarah's invitation copy in the voice approved by Liz.
     Outcome: Mitigates the HIGH-severity opt-in risk by framing this as low-lift micro-volunteering, not lifelong mentorship.
  10. Hidden Co-op Opportunity Surfacing
     Trigger: Sarah mentions in-thread that her fintech startup is hiring.
     Flow: Step 1: A named-entity classifier detects an opportunity mention. Step 2: A Copilot chip asks Sarah, 'Want to formalize this as a referral?' Step 3: If yes, a structured opportunity record is written to SharePoint and surfaced — only to Maya — as a 'warm lead.' Step 4: Maya can mark it interested; the lead is routed to her co-op advisor for vetting.
     AI role: Gemini 3.1 Pro for named-entity extraction; deterministic write-back to SharePoint via Power Automate.
     Outcome: Activates the 'hidden co-op market' the consulting brief promises — without violating consent.

KEY SCREENS (10) — every screen is a real view, not a placeholder:
  1. Teams App Home — Trailblazer Match Tab — purpose: Anchor the entire experience inside the Teams chrome Maya already lives in. No new login, no new domain.
     Primary element: A Fluent 2 hero card titled 'Your week 3 check-in, Maya' with the CLR radar and a single primary action: Find a Trailblazer.
     Motion character: Restrained. A gentle fade-in on tab activation; the radar's amber bands pulse once at 0.6 opacity, then settle.
  2. My CLR Skill Profile — purpose: Make Maya's skill landscape legible without making it feel like a report card.
     Primary element: Six-band CLR radar with annotated cohort-percentile bars and a 'this is normal' contextual ribbon.
     Motion character: Each band animates in sequenced 80ms increments — feels like a polite reveal, not a verdict.
  3. Match Cards with Explainability — purpose: Present three alumni as humans with stories, not as profile photos in a directory.
     Primary element: Three vertically-stacked cards, each with a portrait photo (Imagen-generated, consented), grad year, one-line rationale, and a similarity ribbon.
     Motion character: Cards rise from below with a 240ms ease-out stagger. Hover reveals the trajectory chart with a soft side-slide.
  4. Trajectory Comparison Detail — purpose: Show Maya the specific CLR overlap points so the match is provable, not magical.
     Primary element: Side-by-side timeline — Sarah's freshman fall on the left, Maya's current state on the right, with three highlighted overlap moments.
     Motion character: Overlap dots draw connecting arcs between timelines on entry; the explanatory paragraph types in at 30ms/char.
  5. FERPA Double Opt-In Modal — purpose: Make consent a visible, dignified moment — not a dark-pattern checkbox.
     Primary element: A Fluent modal with three plain-language consent items, an explicit list of what is NOT shared, and a 'Why we ask' expandable explainer.
     Motion character: Modal arrives with a slight scale-up from 0.96 to 1.0 and a subtle backdrop blur. No urgency cues.
  6. Copilot Intro Composer — purpose: Lower the activation energy of the first message to near-zero while preserving Maya's voice.
     Primary element: A composer pre-filled with a grounded draft, a tone slider (warm ↔ professional), and a Verbalized-Sampling 'Show 2 alternates' affordance.
     Motion character: Draft text streams in token-by-token at Claude-realistic cadence; tone slider re-streams variants in <1.5s.
  7. Active Conversation Thread in Teams — purpose: Show the product working inside the native Teams thread UI — no app-switch, no novelty.
     Primary element: Standard Teams 1:1 thread with Maya and Sarah, plus an unobtrusive Copilot 'Suggest a reply' chip under the compose box.
     Motion character: Pure Teams native. The Copilot chip is the only non-Teams element and pulses once on appearance.
  8. Alumni-Side Capacity Dashboard — purpose: Honor alumni time so the opt-in flywheel keeps spinning.
     Primary element: A simple weekly-capacity slider (1–4 active matches), an upcoming-match preview, and a 'pause for the month' toggle.
     Motion character: Slider has a satisfying tactile snap; pause toggle slides with a 200ms ease.
  9. Advisor Outcomes View (Power BI Embed) — purpose: Give Liz a defensible, board-ready view of the pilot's signal without exposing individual conversations.
     Primary element: A Power BI tile grid: matches made, double opt-in rate, alumni engagement delta vs. NU Source baseline, hidden-opportunity referrals.
     Motion character: Tiles load with the standard Power BI shimmer; the Copilot-narrative panel types in the weekly readout.
  10. Liz & Jen Guardrail Review — purpose: Make the constraint-honoring visible — Liz approves templates, Jen sees cost.
     Primary element: A two-pane review screen — left: pending Copilot template variants awaiting Liz approval; right: Azure OpenAI token spend trend with Jen's threshold line.
     Motion character: Approval cards swipe right (approve) or left (revise) with a SharePoint-style toast confirmation.

AI CAPABILITIES (8) — every one wires to a real /api/ai/* endpoint via the multi-provider fallback helper:
  1. Azure OpenAI semantic vector search over CLR corpus (HEADLINE)
     User action: Maya taps 'Find a Trailblazer' on her CLR snapshot.
     Model: Gemini 3.1 Pro
     Input: Maya's CLR vector (skill band amplitudes, course-week position, cohort context) plus the SharePoint-indexed alumni CLR corpus (~1,247 opted-in vectors).
     Output: Ranked list of top-N alumni by trajectory similarity with per-dimension contribution scores.
     User benefit: The match is not based on prestige or major — it is based on the actual shape of a shared struggle.
  2. Match-rationale explainer (grounded generation)
     User action: Maya expands a match card.
     Model: Claude Opus 4.7
     Input: The matched alum's CLR milestones (opted-in subset only), Maya's current CLR snapshot, and the per-dimension similarity scores.
     Output: A one-line headline plus a three-sentence grounded rationale with inline citations to the source milestones.
     User benefit: Maya understands why this person, not just that they exist — building the trust required to hit Connect.
  3. Copilot intro-message drafting (with Verbalized Sampling)
     User action: Maya completes the double opt-in and lands in the composer.
     Model: Claude Opus 4.7
     Input: Approved template library (Liz-reviewed), the match rationale, Maya's expressed tone preference, FERPA-permitted context.
     Output: Three tone-distinct draft variants (warm / balanced / professional), each with a confidence score; the highest-confidence variant is shown by default.
     User benefit: The hardest message of Maya's college life writes itself in her voice.
  4. Conversation-prompt suggester
     User action: Maya stares at the compose box after Sarah replies.
     Model: Gemini 3.1 Pro
     Input: Last 3 messages in the thread (no CLR data), Maya's accepted tone preference.
     Output: Three short prompt-starters as tappable chips.
     User benefit: The conversation never stalls at the moment Maya feels most awkward.
  5. Sensitive-content guardrail classifier
     User action: Background, runs on every draft and reply.
     Model: Gemini 3.1 Pro
     Input: Outgoing draft text, message metadata.
     Output: Pass / soft-warn / hard-block decision with explainable reason codes routed to Liz's queue if hard-blocked.
     User benefit: Protects both Maya and Sarah from inappropriate exchanges; mitigates the MEDIUM-severity risk surfaced in the consulting brief.
  6. Hidden-opportunity entity extraction
     User action: Sarah types a message mentioning her startup is hiring.
     Model: Gemini 3.1 Pro
     Input: Sarah's outbound message (with her consent for opportunity extraction set at opt-in).
     Output: Structured opportunity record (employer, role-hint, urgency, referral-availability) plus a Copilot chip offering Sarah a one-tap formalization.
     User benefit: The 'hidden co-op market' the consulting brief promises becomes operational.
  7. Cohort-context grounding (Wiki RAG over SharePoint)
     User action: Maya opens her CLR snapshot.
     Model: Wiki RAG
     Input: Anonymized historical Khoury cohort distributions indexed in SharePoint.
     Output: Grounded claims like '71% of first-years are here in week 3' with traceable source links.
     User benefit: Reframes a gap as a coordinate. Maya feels normal, not behind.
  8. Imagen portrait & visual generation
     User action: Match cards render.
     Model: Gemini Imagen
     Input: Consented archetype prompts (warm institutional portraiture; never likenesses without explicit consent).
     Output: Tasteful, diverse, consented archetype portraits for alumni who chose not to provide a personal photo.
     User benefit: Alumni feel like humans, not initials in a circle.

VISUAL DIRECTION:
  Aesthetic keywords: Fluent 2 institutional restraint. Teams-native chrome — purples, grays, soft whites. Editorial typographic hierarchy (Segoe UI Variable). Data-dense without being clinical. Warmth comes from photography and microcopy, never from gradients or stickers. No new-product novelty — this must look like it belongs inside Teams the day it ships.
  Hero treatment: The hero is not a marketing splash — it is a calm, useful CLR radar inside the Teams tab. Photography of alumni is naturalistic, library-portrait quality, with diverse representation. The 'aha' moment (the rationale reveal) gets a slightly more generous typographic treatment — a serif-paired pull-quote feel — to mark it as the emotional center.
  Motion character: Restrained Fluent motion. Most transitions 200–320ms with cubic-bezier ease-out. The only assertive motion is the trajectory-comparison arc-drawing between Sarah's timeline and Maya's, which signals 'we found you a real match.' Everything else recedes. No bouncy springs. No celebratory confetti.
  Image generation prompts (the prototype should call /api/ai/gemini-image at runtime with these — the runner reads the result and renders it as a hero/empty-state/illustration):
    1. Imagen prompt: 'Natural library portrait of a Black woman in her mid-20s, soft window light, wearing a casual blazer, confident calm expression, shallow depth of field, editorial photography style, no logos.' — for Sarah '22 archetype.
    2. Imagen prompt: 'Portrait of a Latino man, late 20s, civil engineering project site in soft background, hard hat held under arm, warm afternoon light, documentary photo style.' — for Diego '20 archetype.
    3. Imagen prompt: 'Portrait of a South Asian woman, 24, in a hospital data-analyst setting, clinical but warm, holding a tablet, neutral expression, natural daylight, editorial healthcare photography.' — for Priya '24 archetype.
    4. Imagen prompt: 'Abstract minimal data visualization: two overlapping radar charts in Fluent 2 purples and ambers, soft glow at overlap points, white background, vector style.' — for trajectory comparison hero.
    5. Imagen prompt: 'Editorial illustration of a Teams chat thread floating between two abstract figures, with a soft warm light bridging them, Fluent design tokens, no faces visible.' — for the empty-state of the conversation tab.
    6. Imagen prompt: 'Photograph of Northeastern campus quad at golden hour, students walking, used as a soft hero background at 30% opacity behind the CLR snapshot.' — for the welcome tab hero.

     • Recruit 100 pilot alumni Trailblazers via low-lift micro-volunteering pitch
     • Build the CLR vectorization Power Automate job from Banner + Canvas signals
     • Ship the Teams app scaffold (manifest, tabs, single-sign-on)
     • Author the first 14 Liz-approved Copilot intro templates
     Success: ≥100 alumni opted in; ≥1,200 alumni CLR vectors indexed; FERPA audit log operational with zero un-consented data flows.
  2. Phase 2 (Weeks 5-10) — Intelligence — Match, Explain, Compose
     • Wire Azure OpenAI semantic search against the SharePoint vector index

  3. Phase 3 (Weeks 11-16) — Activation — Threads, Nudges, Hidden Opportunities

  4. Phase 4 (Spring Semester) — Scale — 100-Student Pilot to Cohort-Wide
     • Scale to the full 100-student Phase 4 pilot referenced in the implementation plan

     Success: Alumni engagement +50% vs NU Source baseline (matches consulting brief target); first-year career-path confidence +30% on pre/post survey.

     System: Loading state replaces the button with 'Searching 1,247 opted-in alumni in SharePoint…'

  3. Maya watches the loading state.
     System: Azure OpenAI semantic search completes; three match cards animate in from below with a staggered ease-out.
     Motion/feedback: Cards rise 24px and fade from 0 to 1; 80ms stagger between cards; similarity ribbon counts up. (720ms)
  4. Maya taps Sarah '22's card to expand.
     System: Card flips to reveal side-by-side trajectory chart with three highlighted overlap dots.
     Motion/feedback: 3D card flip at 320ms; overlap arcs draw between timelines at 200ms each. (920ms)
  5. Maya reads the rationale headline 'Sarah '22 hit the same Python wall in week 4…'
     System: Grounded paragraph types in below the headline; citation chips fade in inline.
     Motion/feedback: Text streams at 30ms/char; citation chips fade in at the comma boundaries. (2200ms)
  6. Maya taps 'Connect with Sarah.'
     System: FERPA double opt-in modal scales up over a backdrop blur with three plain-language checkboxes.
     Motion/feedback: Modal scales 0.96 → 1.0 with 220ms cubic-bezier ease; backdrop blurs to 8px. (240ms)
  7. Maya reviews 'what is shared' / 'what is not shared' lists, checks all three boxes, taps Confirm.
     System: Audit-log toast confirms 'Consent logged'; parallel opt-in request fires to Sarah.
     Motion/feedback: SharePoint-style toast slides up from bottom-right; checkboxes animate with a Fluent ink ripple. (380ms)
  8. Maya waits 60-90 seconds (or in demo: skip).
     System: Sarah's opt-in arrives; a Teams notification chimes and the Copilot composer opens automatically.

Thesis: Uses Azure OpenAI to match a student's CLR profile with alumni 'Trailblazers' who had similar early skill gaps, initiating Teams intros.
Description (what gets built):
A networking workflow utilizing Azure OpenAI semantic search over a secure SharePoint repository. It analyzes a first-year undergraduate student's emerging CLR skill profile and matches them with alumni 'Trailblazers' who exhibited similar skill trajectories and gaps during their own first year. Instead of generic alumni networking, the system identifies hyper-specific shared experiences. Once a match is made, Power Automate drafts a contextual introduction and sends it to both parties via Microsoft Teams, explicitly stating why they were connected. This bypasses the dysfunctional 'NU Source' platform and activates the alumni network natively where students already communicate.
Why it matters for first-year undergraduate students:
First-year undergraduate students often feel isolated when facing academic or professional hurdles. Connecting them with relatable trailblazers who overcame identical challenges provides concrete proof that success is possible. This is far more effective for first-year undergraduate students than generic advice from older, intimidating alumni at massive brand-name corporations.

This peer-to-peer mentorship significantly increases student resilience and retention. jobs_to_be_done: When I am stuck on a first-year skill and unsure if co-op is realistic for me, help me find an alum who hit the same wall and pivoted out of it, so I can borrow their playbook without having to be brave first.
success_criteria: Maya (or any first-year stand-in) goes from opening Teams to sending an intro in under 6 minutes with two or fewer composer edits.
100% of student-to-alumni introductions pass through a visible FERPA double opt-in with a logged audit hash; zero data flows without it.
The match rationale is verifiably grounded — every claim in the explainer paragraph cites a specific opted-in field in the alumni CLR record.
Multi-provider AI fallback works under load: if Gemini 3.1 Pro times out, the prototype transparently falls back to Claude Opus 4.7 with no visible error.
Alumni engagement KPI (matches completed per opted-in alum per month) lands ≥50% above the NU Source legacy baseline by week 10 of the pilot.
Liz and Jen can each name, unprompted, the screen that earns their constraint trust — Liz on the consent modal, Jen on the cost dashboard.
Verbalized Sampling on the intro composer produces three meaningfully tone-distinct variants in <1.5s per slider change, and the chosen variant is logged for template learning.

hard_constraints.brand: Microsoft Fluent 2 + Northeastern visual restraint. No new product brand. The product is a 'Trailblazer Match' feature of the existing Teams app — not its own brand.
other: MUST visually inhabit the Microsoft 365 chrome (Teams shell, SharePoint references, Power Automate badges, Power BI embed).
MUST NOT introduce a standalone domain, login, or platform — every screen lives inside Teams.
MUST show FERPA double opt-in as a visible, dignified moment — never a dark-pattern checkbox.
MUST NOT reproduce any research quote verbatim; testimonial-style strings must stay under 80 chars and be distilled.
MUST surface cost containment as a visible artifact (Jen's threshold line on the Azure OpenAI spend chart).
MUST name the existing systems (NUworks, Canvas, Banner, SharePoint, Teams) explicitly in copy where they appear in the data flow.
MUST honor the divergence axis: this is peer-to-peer mentorship matching, NOT employer-document drafting. No resume/cover-letter screens.

Staggered rise from below implies depth and a curated, human-centric presentation rather than a flat directory.

ai_flows.system_prompt_outline: You are an academic data assistant. Ground the student's CLR gap in historical cohort data to normalize their experience.
ai_flows.user_message_template: Student is in week {{courseWeek}} of {{course}}. Their CLR vector shows a gap in {{gapBands}}. Fetch historical percentile data for this cohort.

ai_flows.system_prompt_outline: You are a matching engine. Perform cosine similarity between the student's CLR vector and the opted-in alumni corpus. Rank by trajectory similarity, not prestige.
ai_flows.user_message_template: Match student vector {{clrVector}} against alumni corpus. Return top 3 matches with per-dimension contribution scores.

ai_flows.system_prompt_outline: Generate a tasteful, diverse, consented archetype portrait for alumni who chose not to provide a personal photo.
ai_flows.user_message_template: Natural library portrait of a {{demographic_hint}}, soft window light, confident calm expression, editorial photography style, no logos.

ai_flows.system_prompt_outline: You are an empathetic career advisor. Explain why this student and this alum are a match based on their shared CLR struggles. Cite specific milestones.
ai_flows.user_message_template: Student gap: {{student_gap}}. Alum first-year struggle: {{alum_struggle}}. Alum pivot: {{alum_pivot}}. Write a one-line headline and a 3-sentence rationale with citations.

ai_flows.system_prompt_outline: You are a Copilot drafting a peer-to-peer intro message. Use the approved template library. Adjust tone based on user preference. Keep it under 80 words.
ai_flows.user_message_template: Draft an intro from {{student_name}} to {{alum_name}}. Shared struggle: {{struggle}}. Tone: {{tone_preference}}. Use template {{template_id}}.

ai_flows.system_prompt_outline: You are a safety guardrail. Scan the outgoing message for inappropriate content, PII violations, or deviation from approved mentorship boundaries.
ai_flows.user_message_template: Analyze this message: '{{draft_text}}'. Return pass, soft-warn, or hard-block.

ai_flows.system_prompt_outline: You are a conversation facilitator. Read the last 3 messages in the thread and propose 3 short, context-appropriate prompt-starters for the student.
ai_flows.user_message_template: Thread history: {{thread_history}}. Suggest 3 replies for the student to keep the conversation moving naturally.

ai_flows.system_prompt_outline: You are a named-entity extractor. Scan the alumni's message for mentions of hiring, internships, or co-ops at their company.

A structural rebuild is required to support multi-persona testing and the full end-to-end matching lifecycle.
